title: This wild new PC pro controller runs its own custom OS across a 2.79-inch color display slapped beneath the thumbsticks
summary: Genki says it is "Beyond the Pro Controller".
body: As $70-$100 controllers are only getting more and more impressive, you might be wondering what the pro controller market can do to make you spend that extra $100 or so. It turns out the answer might be to shove a screen on it. Ain't that always the way? That's what you will find on the Genki Manta, a new controller live on Kickstarter . It uses Manta OS, which is Genki's own operating system, and if you're wondering why a controller would even need an operating system, Genki notes that this allows on-the-fly fine-tuning without the need for any extra devices. You can customise its tri-stage triggers, adjust dead zones, change haptic feedback, and more via the onboard screen and OS. And the controller is pretty impressive even outside the whole 'OS and built-in screen' thing. You get up to 8,000 Hz polling while wired (though only 1,000 Hz via 2.4 GHz wireless), a range of over 10 meters, 150 hours of battery via Bluetooth LE 6, as well as TMR joysticks and Hall effect triggers. The 16 MB of internal storage can be used to load apps onto Manta OS, and expandable storage might be offered as a stretch goal, according to Genki. Normally I'm pretty cynical about Kickstarter projects, b…

body: The great Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks continued today with a new video from Leek, and this one is particularly impressive, and damaging, because now it looks like the leaker really does have access to a playable build of the game. Cars can be seen moving on the streets and freeways below, even at great distances; you can't judge too much from a relatively low-resolution video posted on social media, but it looks smooth and steady, and there's virtually no discernable texture pop. title: Screw the wedding photos, I'm playing Doom on a DSLR camera like the good lord intended
summary: Snap and tear? I got nuthin'.
body: The next time you spot someone earnestly fiddling with a DSLR camera at an event, sneak up behind them and take a look at what's going on onscreen. They could be deep in the settings menus—or potentially, blasting through a demon horde in Doom. Yes, it's time to chalk another device up on the "anything can play Doom if you try hard enough" board (via Tom's Hardware ). Github user Lauris-nl has built a module capable of running the game inside the open source Magic Lantern firmware , which in turn runs on the Canon EOS 550D digital SLR camera. The camera itself is an older model, originally released in 2010 and sometimes known as the Rebel T2i. The image processing hardware inside is apparently powerful enough to run Doom at a smooth frame rate, while the image adjustment and menu controls have been co-opted into what looks like a very playable configuration. You get your traditional up, down, left, and right buttons on the radial controls, while the Set button handles "select" and "fire" duties. You can also use the Menu button to, you guessed it, open the menu. It's like DSLR cameras were built for this. Okay, maybe not quite. Lauris-nl says the port is not intended for other cam…

title: AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D review
summary: Not a DIY play, but could be the basis for bundles and budget pre-built gaming PCs.
body: I'm trying not to be too down on the new(ish) AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D . After all, we are living in a time when the regular narrative is that all hardware is brutally overpriced and every tech company out there is trying to make a quick buck off the back of an AI bubble that is ever more certain to wipe out the global economy in one big pop . But here's AMD trying to give us an even more affordable AM5 gaming processor with a lovely dollop of the 3D V-Cache good-stuff. And yet I'm still not happy. I guess, fundamentally, I don't get it. You see, what we have here is a slightly slower Ryzen 7 7800X3D CPU with slightly lower MSRP. On the surface, that sounds great. The 7800X3D was the best gaming CPU of its generation, and only dropped off our recommended list when its Zen 5 replacement, the Ryzen 7 9800X3D , dropped in price. The issue is that the 7800X3D is old now. I reviewed it—very favourably I might add—back in April 2023. That in itself is not an issue; the underlying silicon is still excellent and still performs fantastically well up against the latest from either AMD or rivals Intel. The issue is that it's been out in the market a long while, most enthusiasts have their eyes on…

title: Former Arkane vets' new studio isn't going to try 'trend chasing', and in hindsight, thank God

body: One tragedy about the fall of Arkane Austin—aside from Microsoft's seeming unwillingness to give studios a chance beyond the next quarter—is the pervasive feeling that the studio, whose devs were previously known for their immersive sims, was forced to make something way outside of their wheelhouse. Redfall was a live service shooter, and a pretty cruddy one at that. So it might be buoying news to hear that Dishonored co-creator Harvey Smith and seasoned Arkane vet Ben Horne's new studio isn't going to try and chase down trends. In an interview with The Game Business , Horne and Smith were asked if they thought the immersive sim (which Black Pony Immersive has been strangely careful to talk around), is a dead or dying genre. "If you look back through those games," says Smith, "There are a lot of titles that people still talk about 10 or 20 years later. They have a lot of cultural cachet. And there are a few, if you look at BioShock or Deus Ex or Dishonored, that make a lot of money." Will that change the way it does business or encourage it to rely on the formula that's gotten it where it is? body: The developers at Guerilla Games are making a last-minute pivot for their live service co-op game set in the Horizon universe after receiving negative player feedback during recent playtests, Bloomberg reports. Horizon Hunters Gathering was supposed to be a live service co-op action game where you group up as a team of animated heroes and fight mechanical beasts. Players reacted poorly to it over the three playtests earlier this year—one of which had to compete with Marathon's server slam weekend that was going on at the same time. Instead of pulling the plug on it, like Sony has done to several live service games , it gave the studio several months to reboot it into a regular co-op game with a story and a smaller scope. According to Bloomberg's sources, Sony told the team earlier today that it will need to impress executives with their next milestone in December. If it fails to wow anyone by then, Horizon Hunters Gathering might join the graveyard of canceled live service Sony games. body: Grab a bucket, because GTA 6 is springing leaks in every direction. There's electricity in the air around GTA 6—easily the most anticipated game in history—but I wasn't actually excited to play it until yesterday, when one of the leaked clips (which we won't be linking here, but isn't difficult to find) showed Jason, one of the game's dual protagonists, climbing into a car. As he takes control, the UI shows what seems to be status symbols for the vehicle: its HP and its current gas. Heeeelllllll yea. I hope you actually have to pull up to a gas pump and remember which side the tank is on. This isn't really new, strictly speaking. After the buyout was announced, current and former EA employees alike expressed concerns about a potential crackdown on some games, particularly those that are visibly diverse and inclusive, like The Sims. Former BioWare lead writer Trick Weekes summed it up aptly , predicting that "guns and football" will be fine, but that "gay stuff" will likely be out. body: Los Santos Customs I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. They will be perfect human simulacra, indistinguishable from the meaty lifeforms behind the controller. My goal: to make GTA 5's barely-living NPCs an approximation of that. So I installed two mods: NPC Check On Player and NPCs Get Wanted Stars . The former makes the citizens of Los Santos more polite—they will get out of their cars and check you are okay if they run you over. title: Overwatch's newest Emerald rank is like a live grenade wedged between plat and diamond

body: Overwatch season 4 introduced a rank reset and you know what that means, it's every cat, hog, and retired sniper for themselves as players desperately try to claw back to where they finished last season. As if that isn't stressful enough, we've also got a new rank on our hands. Slotted between ranks Platinum and Diamond you can now find Emerald, the answer to the growing skill disparity between Plat and Diamond players. "As we've shown in the past, the majority of our players are in Gold and Platinum," the patch notes read . "So adding a new rank closer to the middle of the skill curve gives many players a better sense of rank identity, a new goal to achieve, and increases fidelity in assessing skill for many players." title: Fired Rockstar workers say you shouldn't boycott GTA 6 for them: 'We spent years pouring our hard work, skill, and creativity into making GTA'
summary: "That doesn't mean we want you to let Rockstar off the hook."
body: Rockstar's been embroiled for some time in a legal dispute after firing 30 unionised workers in the UK , which has, naturally, been seen as union-busting behaviour by those impacted. The workers, who are part of The Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB), have been making solid progress. In June of this year, it was decided that IWGB would be allowed to present its case that Rockstar had allegedly blacklisted its unionised employees —as in, compiled a list of union members—which would be in violation of The Employment Relations Act , which plainly states that you can't compile a "details of persons who are or have been members of trade unions" for the purposes of "treating a person less favourably than another on grounds of trade union membership or trade union activities." The full trial will be held in September, but in the meantime, the IWGB has stated that folks excited for GTA 6 don't have to boycott the game on their behalf. In a recent video , fired employees stated: "We're going to make it easy for you. Don't boycott GTA 6, win justice for the people who helped make it. "We spent years pouring our hard work, skill, and creativity into making GTA. And we want peo…

title: GTA 6 leaks show a game that looks like more GTA, but not a revolution
summary: It sure doesn't look like the reinvention of the wheel(s).
body: The exciting thing about Rockstar games is not that they have the most advanced technology behind them, the best stories, or the most avant-garde game systems. It's the extraordinary amount of work the studio invests into the little details that make up its big worlds. Red Dead Redemption's dynamic horse testicles (they shrink when it's cold) are a frequently-cited example of that commitment to the particulars. A pair of videos purported to be leaked GTA 6 gameplay surfaced online today , and if they are legit (the immediate copyright takedowns suggest as much), they seem to confirm that GTA 6 is more of the same. The short clips obviously can't express the full scope of Rockstar's designs—and we don't know how recent they are—but there's nothing in them to indicate that GTA 6 will reinvent the open-world crime spree. In one, the player shoots some hoops as protagonist Jason. It's cool that a basketball on the ground and a hoop nailed to the side of your house are not just static props. There's a system in place for shooting accurately, and the game tracks the number of shots made. The other clip is a very typical GTA scene: The player makes a reckless turn in a car, gets clipped …

title: Industry legend Warren Spector is retiring: 'I'm feeling like I've done what I set out to do'
summary: The man who helped give us Ultima Underworld, System Shock, Deus Ex, and Epic Mickey is riding off into the sunset.
body: Warren Spector is one of the industry's most storied developers, particularly among fans of immersive sims. His leading roles on games like Ultima Underworld , System Shock , and Deus Ex —and you know what, even Invisible War and Deadly Shadows , which are probably better than you think—established him as one of the field's most admired and enduring names. And now, after doing it for more than 40 years, he's calling it a day. "Let me cut right to the chase. I'm retiring from game development," Spector wrote on LinkedIn . "At least I think so. I've been here before and changed my mind but this time I'm pretty sure I mean it." Spector said he's had a "great career" and wouldn't change a thing, but added that he's coming up on 44 years as a developer, a span that's seen him work on tabletop RPGs, board games, and "more digital games than [he] can remember," as part of teams ranging in size from a dozen people to 800. "I've worked for big companies and done startups," he wrote. "I like to think I've helped some insanely talented people along in their careers. (That last is the most important.) "With all that behind me and with age and health (my business) catching up with me I'm feeli…

title: 'Live-service is a red flag for us': Why one publisher is embracing an older kind of multiplayer hit: peer-to-peer, server browsers, and organic community
summary: Tripwire sees preservation as a responsibility.
body: It's a frustrating thing to watch good games disappear. We've seen it happen time and time and time again: studios spend years on a cool multiplayer thing, bank on it being popular enough to become a live-service hit, then toss the entire project into the trash when that doesn't happen. That could have been the fate of Deceive Inc , a 2023 'PvP Hitman' shooter that has attracted a passionate, but small community. Developer Sweet Bandits supported the game with substantial updates and microtransactions for over a year, but unfortunately shut down in 2024, leaving fans to assume Deceive Inc would one day disappear, too. Then last month, the unexpected happened : an update on its Steam page announced that not only would Deceive Inc not be going offline, but work is underway on community server tools and mod support that will essentially give the game to the community, and keep it playable forever. The update is not the work of Sweet Bandits, but an initiative of Deceive Inc's publisher, Tripwire Interactive. In an interview with PC Gamer, publishing director Bryan West explained why Tripwire—which also publishes the Chivalry games and makes the Killing Floor series—is going to such l…

title: How to get Chromite in Palworld
summary: Recruit a pal helper, craft a new tool, or go for a much darker alternative.
body: Chromite isn't actually rare in Palworld , but you've got to have a specific tool (or pal) to mine it, which is different from most other resources. To save you from the guesswork, I'll show you how to use a metal detector to get Chromite initially and also a passive farming solution for bigger hauls so you're set up to make your first batch of Hexolite when you're ready. Palworld Chromite location Prepare for a visit to Feybreak Island (Image: © Pocketpair) Chromite is found underground on Feybreak Island , just south of Mount Obsidian, but you'll need to craft a Metal Detector or catch a Smokie to assist in digging it up. Using Smokie's partner skill is the easiest way to farm early on, but I'd recommend crafting a Metal Detector if you have the spare materials. It's expensive to make, but it's much faster and won't take up a pal slot. title: 2 seemingly real GTA 6 clips—and maybe the full map—just leaked online
summary: B-b-b-b-b-basketball.
body: Two seemingly genuine Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay clips are making the rounds online. The first, a minute-long clip originally posted by a group or individual named "Cyberleek", is already being reposted in multiple places, but we first noticed it via gaming forum ResetEra . As of writing, the clip already has more than 100,000 views. In the clip, we see protagonist Jason Duval at an oceanside house—the same one that we've seen in trailers. The player jumps over his deck and onto the driveway, where he picks up a basketball and shoots some hoops. For sinking a basket, the player increases their "Focus" by 2%. We see two cash totals listed in the HUD—presumably one for their on-hand cash, and one for their bank. Another clip, posted almost an hour later, shows the player driving around a beat-up car, crashing into a delivery truck, and then attacking the driver. Elsewhere, Cyberleek has also published supposed screenshots of the in-game map, though art has appears too simple to be how it will actually look in the game. Below one image is a message from Cyberleek, which claims that the leaks are motivated by Rockstar's decision not to release a physical version of GTA 6. The image a…

title: Epic Mickey creator Warren Spector is 'a little bitter' that his studio isn't getting props for sparking Oswald the Lucky Rabbit's big comeback
summary: Oswald, who featured in both Epic Mickey games, is getting an animated miniseries in 2027, and Spector rightly thinks his team should get credit for helping make it happen.
body: Epic Mickey man Warren Spector—also known for other games you may have heard of, like Ultima Underworld, System Shock, and Deus Ex—recently took to LinkedIn to share some thoughts about Disney's upcoming Oswald the Lucky Rabbit miniseries, which was showcased by Jon Favreau at the recent D23 event. Spector said he's "seriously looking forward to it," but he's also a little annoyed by what he sees as the erasure of the game that helped bring the character back into the public consciousness. Favreau provided a brief overview of Oswald's creation in the 1920s during his presentation, relating how creator Walt Disney lost the rights to the character shortly thereafter. While numerous Oswald shorts were produced, the character was utterly overshadowed by Disney's subsequent creation, Mickey Mouse, and languished in obscurity for years. Disney reacquired the rights to Oswald in 2006, and "we've seen him pop up in games and in shorts and things" since then, Favreau said—and, well, that's the extent of it. That didn't sit right with Spector, who made Oswald a major NPC in Epic Mickey, and a playable character in Epic Mickey 2: The Power of Two. "I’m seriously looking forward to it but it …

title: I modded GTA 5 into a life-sim RPG with mining, foraging, a mini-economy, and the ability to fall asleep in the middle of the road
summary: Which is what it's always been missing.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 will, I'm assured, be the most immersive videogame of all time. You simply won't be able to discern reality from fiction anymore. Your gaze will drift from your television, to outside, to the television, to outside, and the sheer fidelity of Rockstar's opus will be such that you can no longer tell the slightest difference between the two. You will utterly lose your mind. It's gonna be great. GTA 5, though? Hardly immersive at all by comparison. If I'm going to successfully mod this game into GTA 6, I'm going to need to rectify that. So I did. (Image credit: Rockstar) I have installed Roleplay Alone , a mod which turns Rockstar's crime sandbox into a sort of pseudo life sim, filled with all manner of strange little jobs for Michael, Franklin, and Trevor to get up to. Thrill as you mine various ores! Marvel as you package and distribute cannabis! Be amazed as you smelt things at a cement mixer somehow! I immediately set about my new labours. title: The new Framework 12 laptop's secret weapon is its battery life courtesy of Intel's Wildcat Lake
summary: Plus some extra goodies like a backlit keyboard.
body: Framework has just announced a new version of its Framework 12 laptop that apparently gets a bunch more battery life. That's despite it keeping the same 50 Wh battery and thanks to Intel's Wildcat Lake processors. The Framework 12 is the company's two-in-one (touch-and-type), low-power, entry-level offering, mainly used for study and light work. Previously it used low-power Raptor Lake-U (13th Gen) processors, but now ones that you pre-order will use fresh—but still low-power—Wildcat Lake, ie, Core Series 3, processors. Framework currently lists a few options to choose from : New Framework 12 options Max clock speed Cores Price Core 3 304 4.3 GHz 1 P + 4 LPE $549 / £549 Core 5 320 4.6 GHz 2 P + 4 LPE $779 / £779 Core 7 350 4.8 GHz 2P + 4 LPE $999 / £999 Those prices are, of course, base prices before adding on the other storage and memory to your DIY kit. title: The 3DMark Port Royal world record has been beaten, and all it took was a $5,000+ liquid nitrogen-cooled RTX 5090
summary: And talent. Obviously.
body: In news only nerds like me will care about (which is pretty much my raison d'être at this point), the world record for the highest 3DMark Port Royal score has been smashed. Shattered. Thrown into the mud. Soundly beaten. Okay, so it's not by a huge amount over the previous record. But the new top score on HWBot is a massive 51,663 marks , and was achieved by user Cmaker. Take a bow, you king of overclockers. I kneel at your ability to make a large number go higher than everyone else. In all seriousness, Cmaker's rig is something to behold. The score was achieved using an MSI RTX 5090 32G Lightning Z , a limited-edition extreme graphics card priced at $5,000+ upon release—and for god knows how much if you can find one today. It was also cooled with liquid nitrogen to achieve a top clock speed of 3,623 MHz, 848 MHz higher than the already-massive max "default" speed of 2,775 MHz. As you would imagine, the rest of Cmaker's rig is suitably extreme to match. The CPU is the venerable Intel Core i9 14900KF (water cooled, of course), the 32 GB of Corsair Vengeance DDR5 has also had a dose of liquid nitrogen cooling, and the power supply is a 1,500 W Corsair unit.
